items.reasons: Neither return states anything the repository or the sources contradict: blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/AGENTS.md:15-18, blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/receipt.json:88, blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/README.md:90, S1 and S10 are all consistent with both. The tie-break is therefore rule 16: will both clients' models follow the wording as intended. Both returns replace the past-tense narrative with direct rules. Both keep the two parts of the 'so' clause: keep the nested contract here for the coordinator to integrate (AGENTS.md:17), and leave the enclosing root's actions alone (AGENTS.md:18; receipt.json:88 'enclosing worktree actions not modified'). The difference is the present-tense fact in AGENTS.md:15-16 that project-readiness's installer 'writes worktree-root guidance and actions'. That fact explains the rule. A keeps it and turns it into a scoped rule that names what would break the rule: 'leave that installer, and the root guidance and actions, to the coordinator'. B drops it. A model loading B is not told that running the project-readiness installer writes at the enclosing root, and B forbids changes only to 'native actions', not the root guidance that AGENTS.md:16 says the installer also writes. S1 favours the more specific instruction. S10 says the second client's model can be more sensitive to AGENTS.md instructions, which makes a precisely scoped rule more important. A's attribution of the installer rests on AGENTS.md:15, whose subject is 'Project-readiness', and on receipt.json:88 ('installed project-readiness contract validator'). The adoption installer at tools/adoption/install_claude_profile.py:2 installs user-scope profile assets, not worktree-root guidance, so it does not undercut that attribution. Lines 15-18 do not say who handles the installer, so A's hand-off to the coordinator is new. It is supported by AGENTS.md:34 ('One coordinator integrates. Writing workers need separate worktrees and bounded file ownership.'). It also does not conflict with receipt.json:88, which records use of the installed validator, not a run of the installer. The case against A: B converts the 'so' clause more literally and adds no directive, and A drops the words 'reviewable' and 'native'. Neither word changes what a model would do, whereas B loses the installer fact that the current lines carry.
